lines.say: Americans' inflation fears just dropped a full point.

lines.text: In October, people expected prices to rise 4.7% over the next year. Now it's 3.7%.
lines.say: In October, people expected prices to rise four point seven percent over the next year. Now it's three point seven.

lines.text: That's from the University of Michigan's final November survey, and it's the lowest since February.

lines.text: Back then it was 3.4%. After the Iran conflict began, it climbed, staying at 4% or higher from April to October.

lines.text: Overall mood rose too. The sentiment index hit 51.5, up from 48 in October.

post.title: Americans' inflation fears just dropped a full point
post.ig:
Americans' inflation fears just dropped a full point, to 3.7%.
Year-ahead inflation expectations fell from 4.7% in October to 3.7% in November, the lowest since February (University of Michigan, final survey, Nov 20).
The consumer sentiment index rose to 51.5 from 48.
Survey director Joanne Hsu pointed to falling gas prices and a better post-election outlook. Lower- and middle-wealth households felt better; those with the largest stockholdings felt worse amid stock market swings.
Long-run expectations eased to 3.3% from 3.5%.
Sources: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, Axios, Kitco.
